takeaways: Many of the best values in the Twin Cities sit just outside the I-494/I-694 beltway, where buyers find newer homes, more land and less competition. The metro median was about $390,000 in 2025, with about 2.5 months of supply.

North: Blaine (National Sports Center), Andover, Ramsey, Rogers (a newer I-94 interchange at Dayton Parkway), Anoka and Elk River (Northstar commuter rail and the Mississippi). Strong new-construction value, but the most variable commutes.

East: Woodbury (median about $410,000 in November 2025), White Bear Lake (historic downtown on the lake, about $435,000 to $457,000), Stillwater (the state's oldest city, on the St. Croix) and Cottage Grove (about $380,000, with lots of new construction).

South: Lakeville (median about $514,000 in July 2025), Prior Lake (about $526,000 to $532,000, real lake living), Shakopee (about $405,000, with Valleyfair, Canterbury Park and Mystic Lake nearby), Rosemount (about $436,000) and Farmington (about $403,000).

West: St. Michael and Albertville on I-94, Waconia on its 3,200-acre lake with wineries nearby, Delano and Hanover for space and quiet, and Victoria near Lake Minnetonka at about $500,000 to $580,000. Commutes run about 35 to 55 minutes.
Jason's ranking of the quadrants: East first, narrowly ahead of South, then West, then North. The best one is whichever fits your commute, lifestyle and budget.
Prices are as stated in the video (2025); see the market reports for current numbers.

faq.q: What are the best suburbs outside the 494/694 loop?
faq.a: Jason highlights Woodbury, White Bear Lake, Stillwater and Cottage Grove in the east; Lakeville, Prior Lake, Shakopee, Rosemount and Farmington in the south; Waconia, Victoria and the I-94 towns in the west; and Blaine, Rogers and Elk River in the north.

faq.q: How long is the commute from Waconia to Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 45 to 55 minutes via Highway 5 and Highway 212, according to the video.

takeaways: The Twin Cities market is split by home type and location. With about two months of supply and a median around $390,000 (up 3%), it's the most balanced market in about five years, but some segments are hot and others cold.

Buyers have leverage in five segments: dated split-levels from the 1960s to 1990s (new construction with builder rate buydowns can cost the same monthly), townhomes and condos with high association fees, large homes on busy roads, high-end homes with very bold design choices, and downtown and investor-style condos.
In one comparison Jason cites, starter homes sold in about 41 days while downtown condos took about 101.

Sellers still hold the cards in five segments: well-priced starter homes, especially from about $250,000 to the mid-$300,000s; updated homes in established suburbs like Edina, Minnetonka and Wayzata; updated character homes in walkable Minneapolis neighborhoods such as Linden Hills, Uptown and Northeast; classic Saint Paul homes near Summit Avenue and Irvine Park; and well-priced lake, river and view homes.
Buyers in hot segments: be fully ready and compete on terms, not just price. Buyers in cold segments: target listings sitting 60 to 120 days and negotiate for credits, repairs or rate buydowns.
Sellers: price from current pending and active listings, not 2022 prices. In cold segments, price below the competition and fix the obvious issues.

faq.q: Which Twin Cities homes are selling fastest?
faq.a: Well-priced starter homes, updated homes in established suburbs, updated character homes in walkable Minneapolis neighborhoods, classic Saint Paul homes, and well-priced waterfront and view homes, according to the video.

faq.q: Which homes are taking longest to sell?
faq.a: Dated split-levels, condos and townhomes with high association fees, large homes on busy roads, high-end homes with very personal design choices, and downtown condos.

takeaways: A driving tour of Edina, about 8 miles from downtown Minneapolis, with roughly 53,000 residents. Homes were selling in the mid to high $600,000s in about 33 days at the time of the video.
50th and France is the heart of Edina, with about 175 shops and restaurants, many of them unique to the area, and new construction around it.

The Country Club neighborhood, established in 1924 as one of Minnesota's first planned neighborhoods, is on the National Register of Historic Places. Homes run from about $800,000 into the millions, and changes must fit the period style.
Along France Avenue south of Highway 62 are Southdale Hospital, senior and 55+ housing, shopping and dining.
Southdale, the first enclosed mall in the world, is being refreshed with new tenants, and the Galleria next door has boutique shopping.

Edina has about 40 parks and more than 1,500 acres of parkland. Rosland Park has water slides and fishing on Lake Cornelia, and Centennial Lakes Park (24 acres) offers paddle boats and mini golf in summer and skating in winter.

faq.q: What is 50th and France in Edina?
faq.a: Edina's walkable shopping and dining district at 50th Street and France Avenue, with about 175 shops and restaurants on the Edina–Minneapolis border.

faq.q: Is the Country Club neighborhood in Edina historic?
faq.a: Yes. Established in 1924 as one of Minnesota's first planned neighborhoods, it's on the National Register of Historic Places, so additions and changes have to fit the original architecture.

takeaways: Bloomington is one of Minnesota's largest cities, about 10 miles south of downtown Minneapolis, with I-35W through the middle and I-494 along the north. Many homes are within about 10 minutes of MSP Airport.
It's home to the Mall of America (more than 520 stores, with an amusement park and aquarium) and a large job base along the I-494 corridor.
About a third of Bloomington is parkland or open space, including the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge along the river, Hyland Lake Park Reserve and Hyland Hills ski area.

West Bloomington has larger single-family homes and a quieter feel, with a median around $390,000. East Bloomington has more post-war houses, townhomes and condos, with a median around $325,000 and quicker access to retail and freeways.
Most homes were built from the 1950s to the 1970s on established, tree-lined streets, so check the roof, furnace, electrical and plumbing. New construction is limited to small infill pockets.

Bloomington suits frequent travelers and people who want metro access for less than Edina or Eden Prairie. It doesn't have a small historic main street, and I-494 eastbound traffic is a daily reality.

faq.q: What's the difference between East and West Bloomington?
faq.a: West Bloomington generally has larger single-family homes and higher prices (a median around $390,000 in the video); East Bloomington has more affordable post-war homes, townhomes and condos (around $325,000) and is closer to the mall, airport and freeways.

faq.q: How close is Bloomington to the airport?
faq.a: Very close: many Bloomington homes are within about 10 minutes of MSP Airport.

takeaways: Big tech is building AI data centers in three Minnesota areas: Rosemount, Monticello and Becker.

Rosemount: Meta is building an $800 million, 715,000-square-foot AI data center on 280 acres of UMore Park (bought from the University of Minnesota in 2023), targeted to open in 2026, and bought more land across the street in 2025. Xcel Energy is upgrading power to the site at Meta's expense.

Monticello: two projects totaling more than 4 million square feet on about 650 acres, estimated at $2.5 billion to $5 billion, near the Monticello nuclear plant, which received a license extension to operate into 2050.
Becker: Microsoft bought about 300 acres near the Sherco power plant in 2024 but hadn't filed formal plans as of the video.
Why Minnesota: cold air cuts cooling costs, plus prepared industrial land, reliable power, water, fiber and a central location near many large corporate customers.

Housing, as stated in the video: Rosemount homes mostly trade in the low to mid-$400,000s, about 30 minutes from downtown Minneapolis; Monticello homes are in the low $300,000s, 40 to 50 minutes out. Jason expects contractors, suppliers and rental demand to follow first.

faq.q: Where are the new data centers in Minnesota?
faq.a: Meta's AI data center at UMore Park in Rosemount, two large proposed campuses in Monticello near the nuclear plant, and land Microsoft bought near the Sherco plant in Becker.

faq.q: Why are data centers coming to Minnesota?
faq.a: Cold air lowers cooling costs, and these sites offer prepared industrial land, reliable power from existing plants, water, fiber and a central U.S. location.

takeaways: Redfin called the Twin Cities metro a buyer's market (about 18% more sellers than buyers in August) while rating Minneapolis itself "very competitive" (79 out of 100). Both can be true because they measure different things.
Nationally, about 46% of home sales in May included a seller concession, a record for that month in Redfin's data, and sellers outnumbered buyers by about 58% in August.

In Minneapolis, the average home got about three offers, sold in about 23 days and at about 100.3% of list price, and about 4 in 10 sold over asking. About 32% of listings had a price cut, up about three points from a year earlier.

The split is by home type: detached single-family homes in demand stay competitive, while condos, especially downtown, are soft. Central Minneapolis scored 39 of 100, with about one offer and around 75 days to sell, at about 3% below asking.

The pricing mistake behind most stale listings: pricing from sales 90 to 180 days old. Price from current pending and active listings, and be wary of an agent who "buys the listing" with an unrealistic number.

faq.q: Is Minneapolis a buyer's or seller's market?
faq.a: Both, by segment. Redfin calls the Twin Cities metro a buyer's market, but detached homes in Minneapolis still sell in about 23 days at about list price, with about 4 in 10 over asking. Condos, especially downtown, are where buyers have the most leverage.

faq.q: How should I price my home in a changing market?
faq.a: Use current pending and active listings near you, not only sales from 3 to 6 months ago, which can be out of date. Pricing right at the start usually nets more than cutting later.
